newsitem.title: ZAIRE: New Congo rulers close state news agency.
newsitem.headline: New Congo rulers close state news agency.

text.p: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have closed the national news agency while they work out new management and editorial policies, an official said on Thursday.
Information adviser Louis Hamuli said the AZAP agency was a mouthpiece for former Zaire president Mobutu Sese Seko and needed overhauling.

"The news agency has been closed down until further notice. AZAP was working for one man," Hamuli told Reuters. "The agency must become a true national organisation in the best interest of the whole country."
The alliance of Laurent Kabila, who forces took control of the country last weekend and renamed it, has set up committees to look at how to improve the credibility of state media.
"We have suspended all the directors. The measure applies to TV and radio people as well. Here again, a new organisation has to be put in place," Hamuli said.
AZAP's Kinshasa headquarters is virtually derelict. Its foreign bureaus have been closed for lack of funds and its staff have not been paid for several months.
